name: Flock (murmuration)
what: Thousands of boids on the CPU with a counting-sort spatial hash, steered as one cloud: attraction to a player-set target around a hollow core, a coherent swirl field so whole regions fold together, gather (tight ball) and scatter (burst) modes, obstacle and ground avoidance with optional deaths, predators the birds flee in a ripple, wind, and travel along a moving flyway. Drawn as instanced procedural starlings that flap and bank in the vertex shader straight from the simulation's arrays.
use_when: the game has flocks, swarms or schools (birds, bats, fish, insects), or the player controls a crowd as one body

third_party.what: three.js (npm, for src/birds.js and the demo)
third_party.author: three.js authors

good_for: playing as a flock or swarm, ambient birds over a level, fish schools, bat clouds from a cave, insect swarms, a living title screen; up to about 7,000 birds on a laptop
not_for: individual animals with their own goals (use crowds or navmesh agents); walking crowds on the ground; more than ~20,000 boids (move it to the GPU)
how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs meticulai-flock, then import Flock (and colliders) from vendor/meticulai-flock/src/index.js and Birds from src/birds.js; set flock.target from the pointer every frame; see HOW-TO-USE.md
